title: Direct field method for root biomass quantification in agroecosystems
author: Frasier, Noellemeyer, et al.

steps.title: Collect soil cores
steps.instruction: In the field, locate four equidistant sampling points between two crop rows using a ruler or metric tape (first and last points must coincide with the neighboring rows). In very sandy soils, sample the crop‑row points first and then the in‑between points. Moisten the soil or sample when moisture is adequate to prevent crumbling. Using a narrow tubular soil auger (0.032 m diameter) of appropriate length for the desired depth, insert the auger at each point, extract the core, and place each core immediately into a plastic bag. Ensure at least four full replicates per experimental unit (e.g., plot).

substeps.instruction: Determine four equidistant points between two crop rows with a ruler or metric tape; first and last points coincide with neighboring rows.
If soil is very sandy, sample the crop‑row points before the between‑row points.
Moisten soil or sample when soil moisture is good to avoid crumbling.
Insert the 0.032 m‑diameter tubular auger to the required depth (defined by study objectives and auger length) at each point.
Extract the soil core and place it directly into a plastic bag.
Repeat for all four points, providing at least four replicates per plot.

steps.title: Freeze samples
steps.instruction: Immediately after collection, seal the plastic bags containing the soil cores and store them at –20 °C in a freezer until washing.

steps.title: Wash cores and retrieve roots
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen samples if necessary, then wash each core through a submerged 250 μm sieve under running tap water. Collect roots retained on the sieve and those floating on the sieve surface with tweezers. If few roots are present in between‑row samples, pool the roots from that depth interval into a single sample; otherwise keep samples separate.

substeps.instruction: Run tap water through a submerged 250 μm sieve containing the soil core.
Collect roots retained on the sieve mesh.
Collect roots floating on the sieve surface using tweezers.
Pool between‑row roots per depth interval when root abundance is low; keep individual when abundant.

steps.title: Dry and weigh roots
steps.instruction: Transfer the collected root material to a drying oven and dry to constant weight at a temperature not exceeding 60 °C. After drying, weigh the roots on a precision balance, then store the dry material in well‑closed bags or plastic vials in a dry place. The dried roots can later be used for image‑analysis of root length or milled for chemical analysis.

substeps.instruction: Place roots in an oven set ≤ 60 °C until constant weight is achieved.
Weigh dried roots using a precision scale.
Store dried root material in sealed bags or plastic vials in a dry environment.
Optional: use dried roots for image‑analysis of root length or mill for chemical analysis.
